column1: Execution is a pre-existing, strategy-independent market simulation engine that is fixed, stable and out of scope for design.
L4 specifies only the seam, the adapter between C3 and C4, which is where the boundary either holds or erodes.
The adapter performs no economics: it translates, records and reconciles.
A number the adapter needs but does not receive belongs upstream in a view or in the quoting policy.
L4 is impure by nature and is the only I/O boundary in the pipeline.
An OrderInstruction carries IntentId as the idempotency key stable across replaces, Market, ProductId, Delivery, Side, LimitPrice, Volume, Validity and an optional ReplacesIntentId.
An OrderInstruction's limit price and volume are tick- and lot-aligned at C3 and are never re-rounded.
shadowValue and urgency are absent from the OrderInstruction type, so Execution cannot read them, making the projection invariant structural rather than a rule anyone must remember.
An ExecutionInstructionSet carries the Gate, the DegradationMode, the ManifestId, the orders, and the DA bid curves which are monotone.
IExecutionAdapter exposes Submit, CancelReplace, Poll, Subscribe, Reconcile and Seal.
Poll and Subscribe are alternatives normalised into one VenueEvent stream.
Seal is the only producer of C4 and validates before returning.
Project from ExecutionIntent to ExecutionInstructionSet is the only crossing, lives in exactly one file, and the target type has no field to hold shadowValue or urgency.
The full intent including audit fields is recorded to the seam log on the Planner side of the projection, so L5 still receives shadowValue and urgency without Execution ever having seen them.
A comment saying not to read a value is not a boundary, whereas a type that cannot express the value is.
The quoting policy is strategy and belongs to L3.
The adapter receives limit prices and does not choose, improve, peg, or re-price a residual after a partial fill.
A re-price is a new OrderIntent carrying replacesIntentId, produced by the quoting policy from the current fill curve and the unchanged shadowValue, re-entering through C3.

If the adapter acquires a price rule, the shadow-value invariant becomes unenforceable, the executionSlippage bucket stops measuring the quoting policy and starts measuring an untested piece of the adapter, and Execution stops being strategy-independent and therefore replaceable.
The simulator and the live venue share one interface with two implementations.
Simulator latency is deterministic or zero while live venue latency is variable and a source of adverse selection.
Simulator partial fills follow the simulator's fill model while live partial fills follow the real book.
Simulator rejections are a narrow modelled set while live rejections come from risk limits, credit, product state and malformed orders.
The fill-model calibration target is the simulator's behaviour for the simulator and the venue's behaviour for a live venue.
A fill model fitted to the simulator inherits the simulator's biases, and so does everything derived from it: FillProbView's BoundTerm, the quoting ladder, and therefore the executionSlippage bucket.
Recalibration against the live venue is a precondition for live operation rather than a follow-up.
The gap between simulator-calibrated and venue-calibrated behaviour is reported and never absorbed.
intentId is the idempotency key, so a repeated submission leaves at most one live order.
Idempotency by intentId makes retry-after-timeout safe and reconnect logic simple enough to be correct.
Cancel/replace is a chain keyed by replacesIntentId and the adapter never invents an identifier, so Settlement can follow it.
On reconnect the adapter calls Reconcile and diffs live venue orders against the commitment ledger.
At reconciliation a matched order requires no action, a ledger entry with no venue order is re-submitted under the same intentId, and a venue order with no ledger entry is an orphan and a HALT.
Live exposure the engine does not know it has makes every ledger-derived plan untrustworthy, and no mode short of HALT is honest about that.
Re-submitting an intentId yields at most one live order, and violation is a HALT.
There is no orphaned venue order at reconciliation, and violation is a HALT.
The simulator is byte-reproducible given the same instruction stream and seed, and violation fails the run.
limitPrice and volume reach the venue exactly as received, and violation is a HALT.
The simulator sits inside the determinism chain, so it must be deterministic under a fixed seed for the replay guarantee to hold at all.
The simulator's seed and version are manifest fields.

If the simulator is non-deterministic through hash-ordered iteration, wall-clock reads, an unseeded RNG or thread-count-dependent matching, that is a named gap in the replay guarantee for the whole pipeline rather than a local defect in L4.
Closing the simulator determinism gap is a prerequisite for T3 and T6.
Until the simulator determinism gap is closed, any comparison downstream of C3 must state the non-determinism explicitly.
One adapter conformance suite is run against the simulator and a recorded venue stub, and both satisfy the same postconditions.
A divergence between the simulator and the venue stub in the conformance suite is a finding about the simulator rather than an exemption.
A reflection test asserts that no field of ExecutionInstructionSet is reachable from shadowValue or urgency and that Project is the sole construction path.

Idempotency and reconnect are tested by submit, duplicate and submit-after-timeout, then by killing the connection mid-gate and asserting the three reconciliation outcomes are classified correctly and an injected orphan halts.
Fault injection covers rejection, partial fill, out-of-order and duplicate events, and a fill for an unknown intentId which must trip the phantom-fill invariant.

Determinism and fidelity are tested by running the same instruction stream and seed twice and byte-comparing, and by a property test that every price and volume reaching the venue equals the one that left C3.
